Authors: Guzmán E.; Andrés B.; Torres-Polo M.
Title: A cooperative digital twin–multi-agent reinforcement learning for circular supply chains: balanced control across production, logistics, and sustainability
Sector: Generic/cross-sector (circular supply chain; construction benchmark, transfer to discrete manufacturing, process industries, waste management)
Key finding: A five-agent cooperative MARL controller trained in a simulation-based circular-supply-chain DT cut lead time 4.5% and raised OTIF 1.8 p.p. versus no action with bounded cost/CO2 increases, preserved effect signs under shocks, transferred across sectors without retuning; integrated data shifted operations toward lower cost and CO2.

Authors: Kaarlela T.; Alekseev S.; Maljamäki P.; Ikäheimo E.; Kurvinen E.
Title: Digital twin framework for electric truck route and infrastructure planning in the Nordic region
Key finding: Gradient Boosting on 180+ real winter trips predicts electric-truck depth of discharge (R2=0.58; load, torque and weight dominate), feeding energy-optimal Dijkstra routing; a TruckMaker-calibrated digital twin with virtual interface lets planners test charger/fleet scenarios; co-simulation reproduces speed (R2~0.99). Infrastructure analysis remains what-if decision support, not optimisation.

Authors: Han F.; Liu L.; Sun J.
Title: Logistics equipment condition monitoring and prediction based on digital twin and machine learning
Key finding: Three-layer IoT-digital twin-ML architecture for predictive maintenance of distribution-centre equipment (forklifts, conveyors, AGVs): ensemble anomaly detection (F1 0.915), LSTM/RF RUL prediction (R2 0.907), fault classification (92.1%); reported 42% less unplanned downtime and 4.5-month payback; low-confidence predictions routed to technicians, whose corrections retrain models.

Authors: Ivanov D.
Title: Toward Industry 6.0: The Ecosystem Age, superintelligence, viability, and OR-AI symbiosis
Key finding: Conceptualises Industry 6.0 as a digital-twin-driven, agentic-AI ecosystem and proposes a 7-layer OR-AI symbiosis architecture for agentic digital twins (infrastructure to resilience intelligence) in which OR models become continuous orchestration engines, agents autonomously synchronise cross-firm MPS/MRP, and managers define decision rules while validating AI outputs.

Authors: Schwede C.; Schipper L.; Cirullies J.
Title: Enabling Non-Simulation Experts to Adapt Digital Twins during Production System Redesign using Agentic AI
Venue: ICCMB 2026 - Proceedings of 2026 the 9th International Conference on Computers in Management and Business
Sector: Discrete manufacturing / electronics assembly (laboratory IoT-Factory, HSBI Bielefeld; smart product in ~150 variants, mobile robots for parts supply)
Key finding: Agentic LLM system (five Smolagents code agents, ReAct, RAG over OFacT documentation/state model; Qwen3-32B) lets non-experts structurally adapt an event-log-generated material-flow twin of a lab assembly factory via natural language; lean multi-agent, RAG planning and non-reasoning LLMs performed best (up to 100% success), removing expert-authored step instructions.

Authors: Leong W.Y.
Title: Climate-Disruption Early Warning for Malaysian Supply Chains Using Multimodal Data
Venue: ICCMB 2026 - Proceedings of 2026 the 9th International Conference on Computers in Management and Business
Key finding: Simulated Malaysian supply chain CDEWS: RNN and graph-based risk forecasting on fused multimodal data plus a supply chain digital twin for what-if mitigation analysis raised disruption lead time from 8–12 h to 64–72 h and cut logistics downtime roughly one-third, stockout risk and recovery duration in three flood/rainfall scenarios.

Authors: Elmay F.; Kadadha M.; Singh S.; Mizouni R.; Otrok H.; Mourad A.
Title: Digital-twins and machine learning-assisted stable, energy-aware unmanned aerial and ground vehicles delivery in blockchain-enabled crowdsourcing framework
Key finding: Package digital twins (Arrhenius model) plus Random Forest predictions of UAV energy and delivery success, feeding a blockchain-hosted Gale-Shapley allocation, improve QoS by at least 37%, delivery success by at least 45%, worker reputation by 32% and payoff by 22% versus benchmarks; the RF energy model reaches MAE 1.66.

Authors: Saidi C.; Hamani N.; Benaissa M.; Rolf B.; Reggelin T.; Lang S.
Title: Towards Intelligent Supply Chain Reconfiguration: A Framework Integrating Dynamic Knowledge Graph and AI-Driven Optimization
Sector: Generic/cross-sector (reconfigurable supply chain, no industry specified)
Key finding: Conceptual framework only: a dynamic knowledge graph feeds a supply chain digital twin; an AI/metaheuristic optimisation engine suggests reconfigurations that are simulated and validated in the twin before deployment, with actors assessing scenarios; no implementation, named algorithm, or evaluation is provided.

Authors: Iqbal T.
Title: MACHINE LEARNING–DRIVEN SMART SHARING PLATFORMS FOR OPTIMIZING LAST-MILE DELIVERY IN SAUDI ARABIA’S E-COMMERCE SECTOR
Sector: Retail/e-commerce last-mile delivery (Saudi Arabia; pooled courier fleets and parcel lockers)
Key finding: Gradient-boosting demand/ETA forecasts (LightGBM, CatBoost, SHAP) feed OR-Tools VRP-TW routing and CP-SAT locker siting; a SimPy 'Level-1' digital twin only stress-tests these policies. Pooled fleets cut routing cost 65% and lift on-time delivery from 37% to 100%; 25 lockers cut CO2 to 0.06 kg/parcel; SLA holds under Ramadan/weather stress.

Authors: Sahu D.P.; Rathore B.; Iqbal R.S.; Jiang W.; Prakash S.; Singh V.K.
Title: A Hybrid Genetic Algorithm and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Optimized Supply Chain Management Using Edge-Enabled Digital Twins
Venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
Sector: Generic/cross-sector (multi-echelon network of warehouses, distribution centres and retailers; no industry specified)
Key finding: Hybrid GA (global inventory allocation, routing, supplier selection) plus Q-learning MARL agents (reorder, reroute, risk mitigation) in a closed loop with edge digital twins of warehouses, distribution centres and retailers; Python simulations on synthetic plus public data beat GA, MARL, ACO, PSO (fill rate 96.5%, turnover 5.78, stockouts 4.3%).

Authors: Dogančić B.; Rožić J.; Jokić M.; Čeredar M.
Title: Decentralised Manufacturing as a Networked Cyber–Physical System: Formalising Free and Open-Source Software Governance and ML Adaptation for Distributed Robustness
Key finding: Analytical framework: each fabrication node's Cognitive Gateway hosts a digital-twin nominal model whose twin gap trains a GP/neural-network disturbance estimator that automatically corrects control inputs; federated learning propagates corrections. FOSS governance provides redundancy, substitutability and informational persistence, absorbing supply chain (vendor lock-in), regulatory and process disturbances without central control.

Authors: Zhang W.; Yu C.; Newman S.T.; Cheung Ho Kin D.; Zhong R.Y.
Title: A machine learning approach for forecasting resilient material delivery in the construction industry
Key finding: A digital supply chain twin with a Kanban and AI layer running an improved HMM (M3HMM) forecasts construction material/machine delivery delays; on seven real projects M3HMM reached ~90% accuracy, beating LR, SVR, GMM, LSTM and HMM, with alerts ~5 days ahead for contractors' decisions.

Authors: Genetti S.; Scarton G.; Formentini M.; Iacca G.
Title: An intelligent Digital Twin based on machine learning for interpretable decision-making in manufacturing
Sector: Machine tool manufacturing (CNC laser-cutting and tube-processing machines, Adige Spa / BLM Group, Italy; more than half of components outsourced)
Key finding: Action research at Adige Spa: an AnyLogic supply-chain twin drives evolutionary-RL learning of interpretable decision-tree scheduling policies, explained by four LLMs; expert votes steer the search, speeding convergence up to 21% and lowering makespan in 3/5 datasets, while interpretability proved decisive for stakeholder acceptance.

Authors: Ivanov D.
Title: Agentic digital twins: bridging model-based and AI-driven decision-making support for a new era of supply chain and operations management
Sector: Generic/cross-sector (illustrations: Automotive - Ford deep-tier network; Cloud/IT - Microsoft cloud supply chain)
HITL function: Set objectives/constraints; Approve/override; Interpret outputs; Handle exceptions
Key finding: Theorises the A-SCDT (agentic AI + digital twin + model-based optimisation/simulation) via the ICARUS framework: an architecture of data-concierge, co-pilot, LLM role, risk and operational agents around a central human planner; humans lead and validate, AI informs and automates flows, humans monitor anomalies.

Authors: Ozturk, C; O'Sullivan, B
Title: An Adaptive Supply Chain Stress Testing Framework with Deep Learning
Venue: TRANSPORT TRANSITIONS: ADVANCING SUSTAINABLE AND INCLUSIVE MOBILITY, TRA CONFERENCE 2024, VOL 5
Sector: Generic/cross-sector (multi-tier supply chain networks of public and private organisations; requirements from interviews, mainly manufacturing)
Key finding: Conceptual proposal (no implementation or results): a supply-chain digital twin combining a BOM/geospatial graph model, ML disruption prediction, an optimisation decision model and discrete-event simulation with a feedback loop; an ANN metamodel trained on the decision-simulation pair serves as surrogate so practitioners can stress-test without modeling tools.

Authors: Keshvarinia M.; MacKenzie C.A.; Zhao Z.
Title: A simulation-based digital twin model for data-driven decision optimization
Key finding: Simulated DT (Simio DES: five-station plant, five suppliers, (Q,r) inventory, condition-based maintenance) with six ML regressors as surrogates predicting profit of 5,880 mitigation combinations; static recommendations recover 72%/50% of lost profit (32/48-day delays), and real-time state updates at supply arrival change the optimal mix (forklift, reorder quantity, overtime).

Authors: Fatorachian H.; Kazemi H.; Pawar K.
Title: Enhancing Smart City Logistics Through IoT-Enabled Predictive Analytics: A Digital Twin and Cybernetic Feedback Approach
Key finding: Framework combining IoT data, XGBoost/MLP predictors, a digital twin and a cybernetic feedback loop for last-mile delivery; on real data from a UK logistics firm, delivery-quality prediction accuracy rose from 76.3% (AUC 0.45) to 85.0% with the feedback loop; operational decisions are autonomous, humans set objectives.

Authors: Fedorin D.V.; Nastenko S.K.; Polyanichenko D.S.; Sukhanov A.V.; Grishaev S.Y.; Butakova M.A.
Title: Method for Rrecognizing and Generating Three-Dimensional Objects to Create Digital Twins
Venue: International Journal of Fuzzy Logic and Intelligent Systems
Key finding: A GIS-integrated editor with two U-Nets and a YOLOv8-obb detector reconstructs port container-yard topology from satellite images (mAP@0.5 0.95, mean contour deviation -0.153) and exports it to a digital twin's 3D scene; an expert test halved reconstruction labour (20 h to 10 h), with users still correcting contours.

Authors: Bhoite T.D.; Buktar R.B.; Mahalle P.N.; Khond M.P.; Pise G.S.; More Y.
Title: Productivity Enhancement in the Indian Auto Component Manufacturing Supply Chain Through IoT, Digital Twins with Generative AI, and Stacked Encoder-Enhanced Neural Networks
Key finding: Layered IoT-digital twin-generative AI architecture with a hybrid BN-SE-PO model (Bayesian network, stacked encoder, Puma optimizer) for anomaly detection and decision suggestions; a claimed digital-twin simulation of a CNC machining cell reports OEE 65->82%, cycle time -25%, defects -50%, but the twin, data and validation are undocumented.

Authors: Zou Y.; Wu J.; Meng X.; Wang X.; Manzardo A.
Title: Digital twin integration for dynamic quality loss control in fruit supply chains
Key finding: A BiLSTM-attention model inside a five-dimensional cold-chain digital twin, using one pallet-level sensor, predicts in-box fruit temperature within ±0.3 °C (about 60% error reduction vs ambient-only), giving shelf-life errors under ±1.2 days and simulated food-loss reductions of 8.6-15.5%; box-level twins are the most precise unit.

Authors: Badakhshan E.; Ivanov D.
Title: Integrating digital twin and blockchain for responsive working capital management in supply chains facing financial disruptions
Key finding: Blockchain data sharing alone reduces but does not eliminate the cash-flow bullwhip; adding the digital twin (DES + supervised ML generating inventory/credit decision rules) eliminates it and further raises inventory turnover, shortens cash conversion cycles and lowers costs for distributors and manufacturer, with service level unchanged.

Authors: Ivanov D.
Title: From digital twins to supply chain ecosystems
Sector: Generic/cross-sector (supply chain resilience, ripple effect and stress-testing; no industry case)
Key finding: Conceptual extension of the intelligent digital twin to a digital supply chain ecosystem: ontologies plus generative AI let the system build and adapt its simulation models and generate disruption scenarios for resilience stress-testing, within a human-AI collaboration where decision tasks are delegated back and forth (human-in-the-loop, not full automation).

Authors: Mhiri M.; Mkacher H.; Al-Khatib M.; Kharbeche M.; AlNouss A.; Haouari M.
Title: Enhancing Liquefied Natural Gas supply chain robustness through digital twin-driven machine learning models: A special case of cryogenic heat exchanger
Key finding: Proof-of-concept twin (Aspen HYSYS model of a cryogenic heat exchanger + decision-tree surrogate + VAR forecaster) predicts the next operating state and autonomously restores it to the nearest safe state; on synthetic scenarios it detects 52-57% of failures early and cuts cumulative downtime about 30% versus corrective maintenance.

Authors: Xiros V.; Gonzalez Castro J.M.; Fernandez-Pelaez F.; Magoutas B.; Christidis K.
Title: Supply Chain Data Analytics for Digital Twins: A Comprehensive Framework
Sector: Circular manufacturing (food processing; WEEE magnet recycling)
Key finding: A containerized, data-space-compliant analytics service attached to existing factory digital twins adds ML anomaly detection, forecasting and trained regressors (magnet properties) in a juice plant and a three-actor WEEE magnet-recycling chain; outputs stay advisory: alerts and predictions feed engineers who simulate parameters and decide.

Authors: Luo B.; Chen H.
Title: Design of a Geographic Path Model for Dongguan Export Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning and Supply Chain Simulation
Venue: Proceedings of the 2025 5th International Conference on Internet of Things and Machine Learning, IoTML 2025
Sector: Cross-border export logistics (Dongguan electronics/manufacturing cluster; ports, customs, multimodal freight)
Key finding: MARL (Double Dueling DQN agents for manufacturers, logistics providers, ports, customs) trained in a digital-twin simulation of the Dongguan export corridor reportedly cuts cost/TEU 22% vs GA, raises deadline compliance to 94.2% and re-plans disruptions in 43 s; agents coordinate without centralised oversight. Reported figures are internally inconsistent.

Authors: Paul S.
Title: Integration of Digital Twin and AI-enabled ERP Systems: A Conceptual Framework for Intelligent Electronics Manufacturing Services
Venue: 2025 6th International Conference on Communications, Information, Electronic and Energy Systems, CIEES 2025 - Conference Proceedings
Key finding: Conceptual five-layer architecture (physical, digital twin, MES, ERP, AI-orchestration) in which the twin mirrors SMT/PCBA lines and feeds an AI layer that forecasts demand, reschedules production, optimises inventory and triggers work and purchase orders automatically; supplier, OEM and 3PL links run through ERP B2B messages.

Authors: Manoharan G.; Gharat A.; Banu R.N.; Soni A.; Sudhakar K.; Dhanke J.A.
Title: Digital Twin-Enabled Supply Chain Management in Cloud-based Smart Enterprises
Venue: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication, ICOSEC 2025
Key finding: A designed DT-FL-MASChain framework pairs an asset-level digital twin with an autonomous agent at each node; federated averaging trains local predictive models (efficiency label, downtime) without sharing raw data, and agents plus smart contracts trigger maintenance, restocking and routing automatically, with no human approval step.

Authors: Abdullahi I.; Larijani H.; Liarokapis D.; Paterson J.; Jones D.; Murray S.
Title: A Data-Intelligence-Driven Digital Twin Framework for Improving Sustainability in Logistics
Key finding: A distributed logistics DT (Azure Digital Twins + Databricks) streams fleet telematics and ERP orders into an RL job-assignment/routing model; planners accept or reject its recommendations and their responses act as RL reward. Preliminary what-if simulations on 2023 company data indicate a 20-30% carbon-footprint reduction from avoided empty runs.

Authors: Ogunsoto O.V.; Olivares-Aguila J.; ElMaraghy W.
Title: A conceptual digital twin framework for supply chain recovery and resilience
Key finding: Three-phase conceptual DSCT: an LSTM on Kerala rainfall predicts floods (75% accuracy, 84% AUC-ROC); a FlexSim DES of a real four-echelon network quantifies service-level drops under 65%/35% capacity disruptions; an MLPNN trained on the simulation output yields a recovery indicator (epoch of MSE convergence) as decision support for planners.

Authors: Pilutti Namer T.; Tornielli M.
Title: Fincantieri Shipyards Digital Twin Model
Venue: Progress in Marine Science and Technology
Key finding: Fincantieri's shipyard 'twin of twins' (data, visualisation, AI simulation) is being deployed across planning, production and logistics/supply chain, with AI algorithms for weld inspection, sheet placement, truck scheduling/reordering and GenAI operator agents; AI proposes, operators confirm, and change management/training are treated as decisive for adoption.

Authors: Kochnev A.
Title: HOW AUTONOMOUS ROBOTS AND INDOOR MAPPING IMPROVE WAREHOUSE SAFETY
Venue: International Multidisciplinary Scientific GeoConference Surveying Geology and Mining Ecology Management, SGEM
Key finding: A GIS/CAD digital twin of a 7000 m2 Czech automotive warehouse simulated replacing forklifts with three AMRs: risk scores fell ~40%, transport cycle time 28%, human-vehicle conflict zones 42%. All figures are simulated; AMRs are not deployed and the 'machine learning' is never specified.

Authors: Nicoletti B.; Appolloni A.
Title: The Impact of AI Foundation models on the future of digital engineering for logistics and supply Chain
Sector: Shipbuilding/maritime (case: leading global shipbuilding company); framework itself generic/cross-sector LSCM structured by SCOR
Key finding: Proposes a CPPS (5C) functional/technical architecture where a fine-tuned LLM AI kernel with RAG, AI agents and a knowledge-based model drive per-machine digital twins for virtual testing and predictive maintenance; maps FM tools to all six SCOR processes; shipyard case (VFM drones, predictive maintenance, surrogate simulations) reports qualitative benefits only.

Authors: Ziari M.; Taleizadeh A.A.
Title: Integrated data-driven and artificial intelligence framework to develop digital twins in distribution system of supply chains: A real industrial case
Sector: Packaging manufacturing / FMCG distribution (glass and plastic bottles)
Key finding: A three-layer distribution-system twin (physical world, reported data, digital world) with an Elastic Net demand-forecasting core feeding a simulation-optimisation DSS integrated with ERP; in a glass/plastic bottle manufacturer it reports R2 0.86-0.87, MAE 9.2% of mean demand, 85-89% service levels and 22% better forecast accuracy.

Authors: Monizza G.P.; Mozaffari M.; Fabbrizzi S.; Gamper J.; Lanz O.; Matt D.T.
Title: Defining a Cognitive Digital Twin architecture in food supply chains: the early outcomes of DSS4LCO initiative
Venue: Proceedings of the International Food Operations and Processing Simulation Workshop, FOODOPS
Sector: Food/cold chain (food supply chains in general; prototype with local stakeholders only planned, no case yet)
Key finding: Design-science proposal (nothing implemented) of a Cognitive Digital Twin for food supply chains: DT domain (IIoT, VSM virtual model, LARG index, multi-objective optimisation) plus CDT domain (OWL ontology, knowledge graphs, ML engine) intended to decide autonomously, with selective classification (abstention) and active learning keeping humans co-piloting.

Authors: Campos M.G.G.; van Beurden P.
Title: Potential of Applying Artificial Intelligence to Hot Metal Logistics Management
Key finding: Validated digital twins of Tata Steel's torpedo and hot-metal-ladle cycles (within 5% / 8 min of real operation), fed by FEM-derived reduced-order thermal models, let reinforcement-learning agents select ladles/torpedoes and schedule the hot metal route, cutting simulated hot metal temperature loss by 15 degC versus the FIFO baseline.

Authors: Corsini R.R.; Costa A.; Fichera S.; Framinan J.M.
Title: Digital twin model with machine learning and optimization for resilient production–distribution systems under disruptions
Key finding: A closed-loop DT (moving-average lead-time forecast, simulation, ANN surrogates inside PSO) re-optimising SOUT parameters every 30 days kept fill rate near 99%, cut backlog by 81-92% and improved time-to-recover and time-to-survive versus static parameters under COVID-shaped lead-time disruptions, at ~8.7 s per review; no human step in the loop.

Authors: Yang C.; Yu H.; Zheng Y.; Ala-Laurinaho R.; Feng L.; Tammi K.
Title: Towards Human-Centric Manufacturing: Leveraging Digital Twin for Enhanced Industrial Processes
Key finding: A three-layer DT architecture (Data, Knowledge, AI, 3D engines) with an industrial-process ontology was implemented in a lab factory and validated on in-plant AGV/crane transport: an LLM-RAG over a Neo4j knowledge graph answers operator queries in natural language, while knowledge-driven 3D safety zones alert crane operators; latency under 300 ms.

Authors: Badakhshan E.; Ball P.
Title: Deploying hybrid modelling to support the development of a digital twin for supply chain master planning under disruptions
Key finding: Hybrid DES-CART decision tree-MIP framework (a digital-twin precursor with periodic physical-digital data flow) updates the SC master plan under demand and lead-time disruptions; responsive planning raised DC service level (+16.88% for product 1) and cut total cost by 15% versus unresponsive planning.

Authors: Ivanov D.
Title: Conceptualisation of a 7-element digital twin framework in supply chain and operations management
Key finding: Proposes a 7-element SCOM digital twin framework (technology, people, management, organisation, scope, task, modelling) and five twin types; concludes twins are socio-technical systems with continuous human–AI interaction, where analytics (simulation, optimisation, neural networks, ML/RL) is the modelling backbone and decisions stay with humans or pass to AI by design.

Authors: Tang Y.M.; Kuo W.T.; Lee C.K.M.
Title: Real-time Mixed Reality (MR) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) object recognition integration for digital twin in Industry 4.0
Key finding: Lab prototype (HoloLens MR + Azure cloud + MySQL) framed as a warehouse digital twin: YOLOv5-s detects packages and pulls item records (location, order number) onto an MR dashboard for operators (125 FPS, 67.3% mAP). Forecast/risk functions only described; humans keep all logistics decisions.

Authors: Badakhshan E.; Ball P.
Title: Applying digital twins for inventory and cash management in supply chains under physical and financial disruptions
Key finding: Simulation-generated data trained a CART decision tree (83-86% accuracy) whose rules set inventory and cash replenishment policies; centralised planning with these rules cut the manufacturer's cash conversion cycle by 11.1 and 9.5 weeks versus decentralised planning, with and without disruptions; the wholesaler's ordering policy drives manufacturer CCC.

Authors: Khetani N.; Sharma A.; Kulkarni A.
Title: Real-Time Logistics and Warehouse Integration via Networks of the Future and Dynamic Digital Twins
Key finding: A proof-of-concept warehouse digital twin couples Ridge-regularised polynomial regression on real packing data (RMSE 14.72 s vs 19.04 s linear, 89% cohesion) with a grid-adapted A* pathfinder, plus Node-RED/Traccar/RFID and 5G, to auto-release orders and re-route AGVs after layout changes.

Authors: Lim J.-B.; Jeong J.
Title: Factory Simulation of Optimization Techniques Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning for Storage Devices
Sector: Electronics manufacturing (battery management system production line; intra-plant stocker/buffer logistics)
Key finding: PPO agent (Stable-Baselines3 in FlexSim) choosing which item type each router pulls from the stocker cut stocker average waiting time from 3348 s (FIFO) to 145 s and mean queue from about 272 to 12 items at similar daily output (7304 vs 7058); converged after 3000-8000 training steps.

Authors: Ivanov D.
Title: Intelligent digital twin (iDT) for supply chain stress-testing, resilience, and viability
Key finding: Proposes the iDT: an SC digital twin extended with an AI part (agents' training/learning environment, self-learning, rule discovery from data). Humans define practices and rules, decide (step 4) with iDT support and keep non-standardised situations; AI takes standardised tasks, recommends and extends human metaknowledge; mutual delegation, no full automation.

Authors: Melesse T.Y.; Bollo M.; Pasquale V.D.; Centro F.; Riemma S.
Title: Machine Learning-Based Digital Twin for Monitoring Fruit Quality Evolution
Key finding: A deep CNN trained on 3,968 thermal images of bananas (four grades: fresh, good, bad, rotten) reached 99% validation and test accuracy, taken as proof that thermal imaging can feed a machine-learning-based fruit digital twin that alerts retailers before stock is wasted; the SAP-based twin architecture remains a proposal.

Authors: Leung E.K.H.; Lee C.K.H.; Ouyang Z.
Title: From traditional warehouses to Physical Internet hubs: A digital twin-based inbound synchronization framework for PI-order management
Key finding: A DT/IoT-based framework for Physical Internet city hubs embeds ANFIS demand forecasting and a joint order-fulfilment/replenishment optimisation model; simulation of a 600-SKU forward-reserve hub shows joint, forecast-driven operations cut daily picker travel by 80.9% and reserve-area visits by 79.8% versus standalone operations.

Authors: Martin G.; Oger R.
Title: A Reinforcement Learning Powered Digital Twin to Support Supply Chain Decisions
Venue: Proceedings of the Annual Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences
Sector: Healthcare (drug/pharmaceutical distribution chain: manufacturer, custodian, wholesaler-distributor, pharmacies)
Key finding: A two-phase framework trains a DRL agent (Dueling DDQN, action branching) in a simulated environment that then serves as the supply chain digital twin, recommending replenishment orders for a four-echelon drug chain; the agent approaches and sometimes exceeds base-stock performance, far exceeds a human-like heuristic, but is less stable.

Authors: Greis N.P.; Nogueira M.L.; Rohde W.
Title: Towards Learning-Enabled Digital Twin with Augmented Reality for Resilient Production Scheduling
Sector: Discrete manufacturing (rail parts, Siemens use case)
Key finding: Conceptual extension of the authors' ML-enabled digital twin for integrated production-logistics: AR overlays present ML rescheduling recommendations, KPIs and plan-vs-actual deviations so a human can select or override recommendations outside the model's learned experience; rare exogenous disruptions stay with human experts; cognitive twins are the longer-term path.

Authors: Greis N.P.; Nogueira M.L.; Rohde W.
Title: Digital Twin Framework for Machine Learning-Enabled Integrated Production and Logistics Processes
Venue: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
Sector: Discrete manufacturing (generic OEM with upstream supplier and downstream customer; no named case)
Key finding: Conceptual three-module framework: ML supplier-risk prediction (RF/SVM/kNN/ANN) feeds a shop-floor digital twin whose sense-and-respond ML model recommends rescheduling; the twin simulates and validates the schedule before it is pushed to MES for execution; a transit module cascades delays to customer delivery dates. No implementation or results.

Authors: Nozari H.; Yordanova Z.
Title: A Self-Deciding Adaptive Digital Twin Framework Using Agentic AI for Fuzzy Multi-Objective Optimization of Food Logistics
Key finding: Embedding a fuzzy multi-objective model in an adaptive digital twin whose agentic layer re-weights objectives from the twin state cut logistics cost ~4-5% and waste ~13% and raised service level ~4% versus static weights, with faster post-disruption recovery; the loop selects and implements policies with no human step.

Authors: Ivanov D.; Gusikhin O.
Title: Supply chain digital twin design and implementation at scale: A case study at the Ford Motor Company and generalizations
Key finding: Ford's at-scale SCDT is a federated, three-layer (intracompany/Tier-1/deep-tier) twin whose executed AI is deep-learning-plus-survival-analysis supplier-shortfall forecasting; agentic AI is designed in as an orchestrator of point tools that alerts managers and recommends actions, while final decisions stay with humans; autonomous execution remains prospective (only e-mail alerts run unattended).

Authors: Zhang C.; Wang X.; Liu L.
Title: Next-Generation AI‑Driven Digital Twin Framework for Market Volatility Warning and Risk Detection in Global Logistics Supply Chains
Sector: Global logistics / multimodal freight (vessels, trucks, ports, warehouses, cold chain)
Key finding: Standards-aligned, security-centred AI-driven DT architecture for global logistics: 5G/6G sensor streams pass an edge node to a secure cloud that updates per-asset twins; gradient-boosted trees and LSTM models trained by federated learning detect anomalies and forecast volatility, and alerts go to operators for proactive intervention. Conceptual, no empirical validation.

Authors: Ivanov D.
Title: Conceptual and formal models for design, adaptation, and control of digital twins in supply chain ecosystems
Sector: Generic/cross-sector (illustrative scenarios: tariff-shock resilience stress testing; agri-food cereal supply chain in MENA via the CERERE platform under development)
Key finding: Theory-building paper: defines the digital supply chain ecosystem, formalizes the twin as a control-theoretic decision-support loop (plan, control, observe, adapt) and a cyber-physical framework with a human-AI collaboration space; AI generates/adapts models and scenarios and recommends actions, while humans verify and decide (AI agent is support, not decision-maker).

Authors: Neyra J.; Silva L.; Netto J.; Medina A.
Title: Optimization of Operations in Solid Bulk Port Terminals Using Digital Twin
Sector: Maritime/port (solid bulk / iron ore export terminal, Brazil)
Key finding: AnyLogic agent-based simulation coupled with an Ant Colony System scheduler, validated against real terminal KPIs (deviations under 5%), cut total ship stay time from 199.6 h to 194.3 h in the base scenario (84.8 h with simultaneous yard-to-ship routes), with estimated demurrage savings of USD 130,750-788,969 within about five minutes.

Authors: Shang, W; Wang, YJ; Zhu, AD; Chen, Y; Fu, PH; Li, XL; Zhu, LF; Sheng, JQ; Zhang, B; Yue, J
Title: DigiPyramid: A Multiresolution Digital Twin Framework for Reliable Logistics Management-Conceptualization, Implementation, and Intelligentization
Key finding: Implemented multiresolution logistics twin (DigiPyramid) for a Chinese nationwide logistics firm: RPA aggregates ERP/WMS/TMS data, Bayesian networks and computer vision fill 'breakpoints', 'gray boxes' and 'black boxes', and AHP-derived indicators serve four human decision levels (managers, planners, schedulers, operators); humans keep all decisions, AI only improves twin fidelity.

Authors: Zhou, LY; Leng, SP; Quek, TQS
Title: VerDT: A Versatile Digital Twins Framework for UAVs-Based Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
Key finding: Edge-hosted double digital twin (learned resource-scheduling twin plus PSO path-planning twin, built from GAN-augmented data with attention-based learning and MA-DDPG) plans UAV parcel deliveries fully autonomously; hardware-in-the-loop Gazebo tests show 63.9% lower distribution latency and 10.9% higher successful-delivery ratio than benchmarks.

Authors: Biller B.; Biller S.
Title: Implementing Digital Twins That Learn: AI and Simulation Are at the Core
Sector: Generic/cross-sector (manufacturing; factory and supply chain process twins, examples from semiconductor, battery, healthcare, consumer goods)
Key finding: Conceptual framing of process (factory/supply chain) digital twins as evolving, learning systems built on four elements (Data, Domain, Analytics, Outcome) and three functions (offline model development, real-time synchronization, online learning); discrete-event simulation augmented by ML surrogates, RL agents and computer vision describes, predicts and prescribes actions on factory/supply-chain KPIs.

Authors: Melesse T.Y.; Bollo M.; Di Pasquale V.; Riemma S.
Title: Digital Twin for Inventory Planning of Fresh Produce
Sector: Food/cold chain (non-profit food bank, fresh fruit)
Key finding: A time-series forecasting model in SAP Analytics Cloud (Smart Predict) on the food bank's historical donation and distribution data is framed as a continuously updated digital twin that predicts inbound donations and charity demand, letting operators reschedule deliveries and run what-if scenarios to cut fruit waste; no accuracy metrics reported.

Authors: Shi L.; Yan L.; Shuqing B.; Cuobo Z.; Yuanchong C.
Title: Research on Intelligent Assembly Modes of Aerospace Products Based on Digital Twin
Key finding: A three-layer (hardware/software/application) digital-twin assembly platform for aerospace mixed-line production couples a workshop-level twin (plan, logistics and quality optimization via data mining) with a line-level twin (fuzzy-reasoning model matching driving equipment monitoring, path and inventory optimization); optimized information is fed back automatically to the shop floor.

Authors: Gao D.; Zhao H.
Title: A Big Data-Driven Knowledge Framework for Supply Chain Risk Prediction and Performance Optimization in Multinational Corporations
Key finding: Three-layer framework (ML/DL risk scoring, digital-twin scenario testing, performance linkage) on a synthetic MNC panel: Federated GCN gave the best disruption prediction (AUC 0.94); twin scenarios showed cross-border diversity, digitalization and ESG dampened climate-shock losses and cut recovery from eight to five months.

Authors: Lu X.; Lin Y.; Ng H.; Liu Y.
Title: When Interpretability Meets Efficiency: Integrating Emulation into Supply Chain Simulation
Sector: Retail (Amazon e-commerce retail supply chain: vendors, purchase orders, fulfilment warehouses, customer outbound)
Key finding: SEmulate replaces the computationally expensive OR order-placing optimisation inside Amazon's digital-twin supply chain simulator with monotonic XGBoost emulators plus ML vendor fill-rate predictors, keeping physics-based inbound/outbound logic; runtime falls ~90% (orders of magnitude) with ~3% accuracy loss, enabling rapid, interpretable counterfactual experimentation for decision-makers.

Authors: Ashraf M.; Eltawil A.; Ali I.
Title: Disruption detection for a cognitive digital supply chain twin using hybrid deep learning
Key finding: CDSCT framework whose disruption-detection module (deep autoencoder + OCSVM) reached 97.6% recall, 2.5% false alarms and 7.1-day mean detection lag on a simulated make-to-order three-echelon supply chain; LSTM models identify the disrupted echelon and predict time-to-recovery; outputs inform human decision-makers, who deploy recovery policies and choose the sensitivity/false-alarm trade-off.
